Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
730 PM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 229 PM EDT Tuesday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast. A Frost 
Advisory remains in effect for the Champlain Valley tonight.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 229 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. Cool and dry conditions continue this afternoon into 
tonight, with a Frost Advisory in effect for the Champlain Valley. 
Temperatures trend more seasonable for the remainder of the week, 
with some chances for light rain showers. 

2. Dry and warming this weekend before showers return next 
week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 229 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Cool, dry, and breezy conditions continue across the 
region this afternoon with temperatures generally in the upper 40s 
to mid 50s. West to northwesterly winds continue to be breezy, 
though not as strong as yesterday. These winds will drop off this 
evening, which will allow for temperatures to drop this evening as 
ideal radiational cooling takes place given the dry airmass across 
the region. Temperatures overnight will generally drop into the 20s 
and 30s across the region. A Frost Advisory remains in effect for 
the Champlain Valley, where the growing season is still active. The 
best potential for frost development will be earlier in the night, 
with southerly winds and increased cloud cover putting an end to 
frost potential by 5AM or so. 

For tomorrow, the region will be on the periphery of a low centered 
over James Bay, with an associated warm front passing through mid-
day tomorrow. Temperatures tomorrow will be much warmer in 
comparison to this afternoon, with daytime highs generally in the 
upper 50s and 60s. Some light rain showers will be possible 
throughout the day tomorrow, particularly in the afternoon or 
evening but expected rainfall amounts will be fairly light. 
Additional shower chances will be possible through the end of the 
work week as a cold front moves through on Thursday. Thursday looks 
like it could be quite similar to yesterday, with more convective 
showers developing behind the front and the potential for some small 
hail and/or graupel.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Large ridging over the Mid-Atlantic states is expected 
to roll eastward supporting an increase in ridging over the 
Northeast. Conditions will be around to slightly below seasonal 
averages for Saturday as ridging keeps conditions dry. Sunday, flow 
is favored to shift more out of the south to southwest promoting 
warm air advection and temperatures warming above seasonal averages 
into the upper 60s to around 70 degrees. Winds will likely be on the 
rise under this pattern shift for Sunday with gusts 15-20 mph. 

Beyond Sunday, the high is favored to remain progressive with a 
southern trajectory low pressure system potentially riding up the 
backside of the ridge. This low could be the remnants of a tropical 
system out of the Gulf waters off Texas and Louisiana. However, 
models tend to be too progressive with these features at this time 
scale, so it's more likely that this low will be delayed longer. If 
so, a northern stream trough will sweep through. Either way, some 
precipitation chances are possible.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 00Z Thursday...VFR conditions will prevail through the
TAF period. Skies remain mostly clear through 06z, then mid/high
clouds from west to east thereafter as a warm front lifts
through the region. Ceilings generally to remain AOA 5000 ft
until late in the period, when they may approach MVFR at
MSS/SLK. Scattered showers are possible during the day
Wednesday, mainly after 18z; lack of coverage precluded mention
in the TAFs at this time. Light and variable winds overnight
turn to the S/SW by 12z Wed, becoming gusty 15-25 kt, especially
at BTV/PBG/MSS due to channeling. Low-level jet moving through
northern NY late tonight/early Wed morning will bring periods of
LLWS at MSS/SLK 10z-16z Wed.
